Blueberry Nice is a largely forgotten piece of early hybrid cannabis history, created during an era when breeders were combining established varieties to see how their most distinctive traits would interact rather than building strains around fashionable names. The cultivar originated with the now-defunct Irish Rose Seed Company and was historically sold as Blueberry × Mr. Nice, a pairing of a Blueberry male with a female Mr. Nice. Archived references tracing their information to Ed Rosenthal ‘s early Big Book of Buds preserve that exact breeding direction, while historical seed lists also identify Irish Rose as the breeder.

The resulting weed brings together sweet berry character and colorful flower potential with the dense, resinous, hash-oriented traits associated with Mr. Nice. Today the name is often shortened to Blueberry Nice, and descriptions vary considerably because the original seed company disappeared years ago. That makes careful historical documentation particularly important when separating the authentic cultivar from newer marijuana flowers carrying a similar name.
Genetics and Lineage

The strongest historical evidence identifies Blueberry Nice as Blueberry male × Mr. Nice female. A transcription specifically attributed to the first Big Book of Buds lists Irish Rose Seeds’ Blueberry × Nice in exactly that form, while several older cannabis lineage archives independently preserve the same pairing. The cross also appears among Irish Rose’s documented catalog offerings alongside Blueberry × Thai, Blueberry × White Rhino , and Blueberry × The Real McCoy. This consistency makes the lineage considerably more defensible than modern secondary descriptions that assign the plant an unexplained sativa percentage without accounting for the actual parents.

Mr. Nice adds especially strong indica influence. Sensi Seeds , the breeder responsible for that parent, identifies Mr. Nice as G13 × Hash Plant and classifies it as 100% indica. The company describes compact growth, heavy flowers, abundant trichomes, earthy-sweet spice, and an intense body-centered effect. Blueberry contributes the opposite side of the aromatic equation: sweet fruit, berry character, possible blue-purple pigmentation, and a more euphoric dimension. Taken together, the documented parents make Blueberry Nice more logically described as an indica-leaning hybrid than the 80% sativa classification sometimes attached to modern listings. The original Irish Rose plants may still have expressed significant variation, however, particularly because old Blueberry populations were never genetically uniform in the modern clone-only sense.
Effects and Experience

The experience can be understood as a meeting point between Blueberry’s pleasant mental lift and the heavier G13-Hash Plant foundation of Mr. Nice. Early effects are likely to feel brighter than the genealogy alone suggests. Mood can rise noticeably, conversation may become easier, and sensory activities such as music, films, nature, or casual socializing can acquire a warmer, more immersive quality. Modern reports commonly describe the cultivar as upbeat and sociable rather than immediately sedating, which fits the idea of Blueberry softening the more forceful physical qualities of the maternal parent.

As the high develops, the Mr. Nice influence becomes more apparent. Physical tension gradually recedes and the experience shifts toward a calm, grounded state. Unlike an intensely stimulating Haze, the cerebral component does not necessarily continue building; instead, the body catches up and can eventually become the dominant part of the session. Sensi Seeds describes Mr. Nice itself as fast acting, powerful, deeply relaxing, and capable of substantial body stone, so heavier expressions of Blueberry Nice may inherit considerable evening-use potential. Higher doses are therefore more likely to interfere with concentration or coordination than smaller amounts.
Medical Benefits

For medical marijuana consumers, the combination of mood elevation and physical relaxation may be the cultivar’s most useful characteristic. Cannabis with this type of progression is sometimes chosen by people seeking temporary relief from stress while also wanting muscular relaxation or an easier transition into rest. Appetite stimulation may occur, and the heavier second half of the experience could appeal to consumers who prefer evening cannabis for discomfort or difficulty settling down.

Blueberry Nice itself has not been studied in controlled clinical trials, so it should not be represented as a proven treatment for anxiety, depression, chronic pain, insomnia, or another medical condition. Historical strain names also provide only limited information about actual chemistry. A modern flower labeled Blueberry Nice may differ dramatically from an original Irish Rose plant in cannabinoid and terpene composition. Medical consumers should therefore rely on laboratory results from the specific product whenever available, particularly when THC sensitivity, medication interactions, or underlying health conditions are concerns.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Sweet blueberry is the defining aromatic idea, but the parentage gives the profile more depth than berry flavor alone. Historical enthusiasts discussing the Irish Rose line specifically remembered its unusually heavy resin production, while modern descriptions regularly associate the flower with blueberry, herbs, earth, and sweetness. Properly cured buds may open with ripe berries and fruit skin before revealing damp earth, dry herbs, resin, and a deeper hash-like quality underneath.

Mr. Nice helps explain that darker background. Sensi Seeds describes its aroma as earthy, spicy, sweet, and strongly reminiscent of resin and hashish. In Blueberry Nice, those traits can contrast with the fruitier paternal side, creating a flavor that moves from berry sweetness toward spice and earth on the finish. This is closer to old-school blueberry cannabis than today’s syrupy candy strains: fruit remains recognizable, but it is surrounded by unmistakable marijuana pungency.

No standardized terpene analysis from Irish Rose survives. Myrcene would fit the earthy-fruit qualities commonly associated with Blueberry-type flower, while caryophyllene could support spice and pinene may contribute fresh herbal notes. Those associations should remain descriptive rather than definitive. Growing conditions, harvest maturity, phenotype, drying, and storage can all alter the aromatic balance enough that laboratory testing is required to identify the actual dominant terpenes in any modern sample.
Growing Information

Cultivation information for Blueberry Nice is considerably harder to verify than its ancestry because Irish Rose Seed Company has been out of business for many years. Historical growers still remember the company’s genetics, and one discussion of the original Big Book of Buds entry specifically remarked on the exceptional trichome coverage visible on Blueberry × Nice flowers. That resin production is consistent with both sides of the cross. Blueberry lines can produce heavily frosted, colorful flowers, while Sensi Seeds describes Mr. Nice as forming large, weighty buds covered with glittering trichomes.

Structurally, growers should expect substantial indica influence. The Mr. Nice mother has a thick central stem, bushy lateral development, and relatively limited flowering stretch. Blueberry genetics can add more variation, including plants with greater branching or slightly taller proportions. Topping or low-stress training should work well where plants show sufficient vigor, allowing several productive tops to share the canopy rather than relying entirely on one central cola. Dense flower development also makes airflow important during the final weeks. Keeping humidity controlled around interior buds reduces the environment in which Botrytis and other fungal problems thrive.

A precise original Irish Rose flowering specification has not been recovered reliably enough to present as fact. Approximately eight to nine weeks is a reasonable cultivation window based on the parent genetics—Sensi Seeds gives Mr. Nice a 60–65-day bloom—while traditional Blueberry selections often mature in a broadly comparable period. Outdoor growers should plan around an autumn finish and watch weather carefully as dense flowers mature. Historic yield numbers should likewise be treated cautiously; the genetics indicate good production potential, but specific gram-per-square-meter claims circulating today cannot confidently be attributed to Irish Rose.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Blueberry Nice?

The historic Irish Rose Seeds cultivar was created from a Blueberry male and a Mr. Nice female. Multiple older lineage records preserve that exact breeding direction, including material attributed to Ed Rosenthal’s Big Book of Buds .
Who bred Blueberry Nice?

Irish Rose Seed Company created the original strain, which was generally marketed as Blueberry × Mr. Nice or Blueberry × Nice. The company later disappeared, and original seed stock became increasingly difficult to locate. Older grower discussions specifically identify Irish Rose as defunct and remember the Blueberry × Nice entry in period strain literature.
Is Blueberry Nice a sativa or indica?

It is best treated as an indica-leaning hybrid based on its documented genetics. Mr. Nice is a pure-indica G13 × Hash Plant cultivar according to Sensi Seeds, and classic Blueberry also carries substantial indica influence. Modern claims describing Blueberry Nice as 80% sativa are difficult to reconcile with this documented parentage.
What does Blueberry Nice taste like?

Expect blueberry and sweet mixed fruit supported by herbal, earthy, spicy, and hash-like notes. Some expressions may emphasize fresh berries, while heavier Mr. Nice-influenced phenotypes can move toward resin, earth, and Afghan-style spice.
Is Blueberry Nice still available?

Authentic Irish Rose seed stock is exceptionally uncommon because the original company closed years ago. Plants or flower carrying the Blueberry Nice name today may be recreations, preserved selections, or unrelated crosses, so provenance matters when trying to locate the historical cultivar.
Final Thoughts on Blueberry Nice

Blueberry Nice is most interesting when viewed as a historical cannabis strain rather than through the simplified descriptions that later accumulated around the name. Irish Rose Seeds took a Blueberry male and paired it with a female Mr. Nice, combining fruit-forward Blueberry traits with one of Sensi Seeds’ heaviest G13 × Hash Plant indicas. The original cross earned enough recognition to appear in period strain references, and experienced growers still remember Irish Rose genetics decades after the seed company disappeared.

Sweet berry flavor may be the easiest characteristic to advertise, but the deeper appeal lies in the contrast between fruit and old-school hash genetics. Resinous flowers, earthy spice, potential blue coloration, a pleasant cerebral opening, and a progressively heavier body effect create a profile far removed from today’s candy-focused Blueberry hybrids. Because original seeds are now scarce and breeder cultivation records are incomplete, claims about exact THC percentages , yields, or flowering dates deserve caution. What can be documented with confidence is the part that matters most: Blueberry Nice was an Irish Rose Seeds creation built from Blueberry and Mr. Nice, and it remains an intriguing artifact from an earlier generation of marijuana breeding.
